Subject: PayGrid model-fit eval & parity follow-up

Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: validate whether open models can reach parity with PayGrid's proprietary baseline for "invoice classification + entity extraction" while meeting latency and cost targets.
- Success criteria you mentioned: match baseline F1 on key entities (~95% of current baseline) and keep 99th-percentile latency under 120ms for typical request sizes.
- Risks you flagged: sensitive PII in the dataset and potential regression on rare entity classes.

Proposed immediate next steps (items we can start on this week):
1) You share a small anonymized dataset sample (500-1,000 records) and an exported evaluation script or metric definition (how you compute per-entity F1).
2) We run a fast model-fit eval with 3 open variants + our recommended Redwood-verified baseline and share a parity report.
3) If parity looks promising, move to a longer-run eval (full dataset) and discuss deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated) and SLA requirements.

I attached a one-page eval plan and a sample prompt set we typically use. See attached: prompt_sets_v1.jsonl and open_model_benchmark.pdf. Also sharing the Drive folder for full results once they arrive.

Let me know when you can share the sample and any redaction requirements for PII — we can sign an additional DPA or accept an anonymized CSV export.

Thanks,
Lauren

Alex —

Great, thanks for the quick response. To answer your questions and set expectations: 

1) Scoring & match windows
- We'll accept both strict per-entity F1 and a relaxed matching variant. For parity decisions, we typically require >=95% of your baseline F1 on the strict scorer OR >=97% on a relaxed scorer; either condition plus no major regression on low-frequency entities will be treated as pass.

2) Data format
- CSV with (id, text, entities-json) is perfect. If possible include a small column indicating "sensitivity_tag" for rows with PII so we can confirm redaction.

3) Models we plan to evaluate (initial quick run):
- Redwood-Opt-3B-quant (our quantized variant, cost-efficient)
- Llama-3-7B-open (baseline open model)
- Mistral-7B-instruct (open instruction-tuned)
- Redwood-Verified-7B (internal Redwood baseline tuned for extraction tasks)

We’d run the quick run on a 1k sample: tokenization + inference + your evaluation script. Expect a turnaround of 48 hours after we receive the dataset (fast pass) with an initial parity report (CSV + concise slide). If we see parity gaps, we will run prompt-set tuning and light instruction fine-tuning on a holdout subset and re-evaluate.

4) Quality/regression concerns
- For rare entities (those <1% frequency) we will report per-entity counts and confidence intervals. If we observe >5% absolute drop on any critical entity, we'll flag it as a regression and propose mitigation (fallback to proprietary baseline for those classes or targeted fine-tuning).

5) Security: please add redaction guidance in the data export; if needed we can accept a synthetic/obfuscated sample. We are happy to sign a DPA or team up with your security folks; happy to take that offline.

Links & prelim materials: 
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-paygrid-evals (we'll populate with the parity report)
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/PG-2027-0423

I attached the evaluation checklist and initial prompt sets used for extraction.

Next steps: if you confirm Thursday for sample delivery, we will triage and confirm the 48-hr fast pass window.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Alex — quick technical note from the ML side: 

- Metrics: please include micro and macro F1, precision/recall per entity, and a token-level exact-match score if you have it. That helps diagnose skew where long multi-token entities are failing.
- Eval variants: we will run both zero-shot (prompting) and a light instruction-tune (few epochs on 500 examples) where allowed. For the quantized Redwood-Opt-3B-quant we expect ~2-3x cost improvement vs full fp16 at small latency impact due to kernel optimizations.
- Infrastructure: for the 48-hr fast pass we will run on Hosted capacity; if the full dataset run is needed we recommend Dedicated to hit the 99th pctl latency SLO.
- Files: please send CSV + your evaluation script (python or a small notebook) and any artifact listing how you compute entity spans. Preferably include an example row and expected scored output.

If you want, we can also include a quick parity visualization (per-entity bar chart + calibration plots) in the initial report.

—Aditya

Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
